name: Question 20
problem:
Jack, a basketball player, practices performing several sets of two free throws. The results are shown below. Based on this data, if the random $X$ represents the number of baskets he makes in a randomly selected set, what is $\text{SD}[X]?$

| Number of baskets | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Frequency | $1$ | $8$ | $16$ |
worked_solution:
The standard deviation of a random variable $X$ is defined as

$$
\text{SD}[X]=\sqrt{\text{Var}[X]},
$$

where the variance can be computed using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

First, we need to compute the probability mass function $f(x).$ To do this, we divide each frequency by the total, which is $1+8+16=25.$ We get the following result:

| $x$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $\frac{1}{25}$ | $\frac{8}{25}$ | $\frac{16}{25}$ |

Now, we compute $\text{E}[X]$ by summing up the products of each value of $X$ and its associated probability:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & =0\cdot f(0)+1\cdot f(1)+2\cdot f(2) \\  & =0(\frac{1}{25})+1(\frac{8}{25})+2(\frac{16}{25}) \\  & =\frac{8}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}].$ Summing up the products of each value of ${X}^{2}$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={0}^{2}\cdot f(0)+{1}^{2}\cdot f(1)+{2}^{2}\cdot f(2) \\  & =0(\frac{1}{25})+1(\frac{8}{25})+4(\frac{16}{25}) \\  & =\frac{72}{25}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the variance is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =\frac{72}{25}-{(\frac{8}{5})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{72}{25}-\frac{64}{25} \\  & =\frac{8}{25}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{SD}[X] & =\sqrt{\text{Var}[X]} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{8}{25}} \\  & =\frac{2\sqrt{2}}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 20
?

Jack, a basketball player, practices performing several sets of two free throws. The results are shown below. Based on this data, if the random X represents the number of baskets he makes in a randomly selected set, what is SD[X]?

Number of baskets 0 1 2
Frequency 1 8 16
a
25
b
225
c
522
d
52
e
255
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The standard deviation of a random variable X is defined as

SD[X]=Var[X],

where the variance can be computed using the following formula:

Var[X]=E[X2]−E[X]2

First, we need to compute the probability mass function f(x). To do this, we divide each frequency by the total, which is 1+8+16=25. We get the following result:

x 0 1 2
f(x) 125 825 1625

Now, we compute E[X] by summing up the products of each value of X and its associated probability:

E[X]=0⋅f(0)+1⋅f(1)+2⋅f(2)=0(125)+1(825)+2(1625)=85

Then, we compute E[X2]. Summing up the products of each value of X2 and its associated probability, we get

E[X2]=02⋅f(0)+12⋅f(1)+22⋅f(2)=0(125)+1(825)+4(1625)=7225.

So, the variance is given by

Var[X]=E[X2]−E[X]2=7225−(85)2=7225−6425=825.

Finally,

SD[X]=Var[X]=825=225.
